                                                                          A comment whose lines changed since it was written moves to the top of its file with GitHub’s “Outdated” and the code it was written on. On the Summary it keeps its link, which now goes to that thread. A comment of the AI’s that the new code fixes is resolved by the AI (decision 12) and shows in GitHub’s resolved look; you can open it, reply or unresolve it. Until Submit review sends it, the resolve is pending: GitHub’s “Pending” tag sits on its resolved line, in the step and on the Summary. On your own change there is no code host, so the resolve stays on the page with no “Pending”.

                                                                                                                                                  Keyboard New

                                                                                                                                                  GitHub’s keys where it has them: J and K move to the next and previous file, through every step in reading order; C opens the changes switch. V marks the file you are on Viewed. No list of keys and no ? sheet: each key shows only in the tooltip of the control it presses, and J and K need none, as on GitHub. The key is written in brackets, as Finish review already does with “Go to the Summary (G S)”. The file you are on carries the focus ring, in the diff and in the step list.

                                                                                                                                                              Comments and threads

                                                                                                                                                              One comment component for everyone. The AI’s comments carry the AI avatar and [AI]; yours carry your avatar; both say Pending and have Edit and Delete until you submit. Colleagues’ threads have Reply and Resolve. Ask AI lives in a thread and on picked lines; the question and its answer stay on the page and never go out.

                                                                                                                                                              Mascot

                                                                                                                                                              The AI, drawn as itself. One character in one construction, eight expressions, four scenes, two sizes of head, and a short set of rules. Every drawing uses the page tokens, so it follows light and dark. The files are in brand/mascot/.

                                                                                                                                                              The character

                                                                                                                                                              Light

                                                                                                                                                              The mascot

                                                                                                                                                              The AI, drawn as itself: the ink square from its comments, given eyes, an antenna, a body and a desk. It shows up where the page waits or says goodbye, never while you read. Working name: Walt (from Walkthrough).

                                                                                                                                                              AI→

                                                                                                                                                              Its head is the AI’s avatar, the ink rounded square on every AI comment. Same corners, same ink; the eyes are what make it a character.

                                                                                                                                                              Dark

It shows up where the page waits or says goodbye, never while you read. Working name: Walt (from Walkthrough).

                                                                                                                                                              Light
                                                                                                                                                              Dark

                                                                                                                                                              Light
                                                                                                                                                              Dark

                                                                                                                                                              Sizes and colour

                                                                                                                                                              Light

                                                                                                                                                              48 and up: the full head with antenna. 32 and below: the head alone, eyes drawn larger, no antenna. Never below 16.

                                                                                                                                                              InkThe body; --tx. Near-black in light, near-white in dark.
                                                                                                                                                              CanvasEyes, mouth, closed eyes; --bg, so the face is always cut out of the body.
                                                                                                                                                              Secondary ink and rulesThe desk, monitor and keyboard; the only other colours are the diff green and red on its screen.
                                                                                                                                                              Dark

                                                                                                                                                              48 and up: the full head with antenna. 32 and below: the head alone, eyes drawn larger, no antenna. Never below 16.

                                                                                                                                                              InkThe body; --tx. Near-black in light, near-white in dark.
                                                                                                                                                              CanvasEyes, mouth, closed eyes; --bg, so the face is always cut out of the body.
                                                                                                                                                              Secondary ink and rulesThe desk, monitor and keyboard; the only other colours are the diff green and red on its screen.

                                                                                                                                                              Rules

                                                                                                                                                              Light

                                                                                                                                                              Do

                                                                                                                                                              • Use it where the page waits, recovers or ends: the Opening, the farewell, a lost session, an empty list.
                                                                                                                                                              • Keep it ink and canvas, in the page’s own tokens, so it follows light and dark.
                                                                                                                                                              • Give it one clear expression per moment, and words beside it that say what is going on.
                                                                                                                                                              • Mark it decorative (aria-hidden) when the words already say it; label it when it stands alone.
                                                                                                                                                              • Stop its motion under reduced motion and when it is offscreen.

                                                                                                                                                              Don’t

                                                                                                                                                              • Put it next to code you are reading, in threads, or in the step list.
                                                                                                                                                              • Colour it with the accent or a status colour, or add gradients, shadows or outlines.
                                                                                                                                                              • Give it props beyond its desk, monitor and keyboard; no hats, no mugs, no seasonal outfits.
                                                                                                                                                              • Make it speak for the AI’s findings; its bubbles are reactions, never review content.
                                                                                                                                                              • Animate it in a loop where nothing is waiting.
                                                                                                                                                              Dark

                                                                                                                                                              Do

                                                                                                                                                              • Use it where the page waits, recovers or ends: the Opening, the farewell, a lost session, an empty list.
                                                                                                                                                              • Keep it ink and canvas, in the page’s own tokens, so it follows light and dark.
                                                                                                                                                              • Give it one clear expression per moment, and words beside it that say what is going on.
                                                                                                                                                              • Mark it decorative (aria-hidden) when the words already say it; label it when it stands alone.
                                                                                                                                                              • Stop its motion under reduced motion and when it is offscreen.

                                                                                                                                                              Don’t

                                                                                                                                                              • Put it next to code you are reading, in threads, or in the step list.
                                                                                                                                                              • Colour it with the accent or a status colour, or add gradients, shadows or outlines.
                                                                                                                                                              • Give it props beyond its desk, monitor and keyboard; no hats, no mugs, no seasonal outfits.
                                                                                                                                                              • Make it speak for the AI’s findings; its bubbles are reactions, never review content.
                                                                                                                                                              • Animate it in a loop where nothing is waiting.
